what_its_for: Penciclovir cream is used to treat cold sores (also called fever blisters) on the lips and around the mouth caused by the herpes simplex virus. It helps cold sores heal faster and reduces pain and tingling. It does NOT cure herpes, but it helps manage outbreaks.
how_to_take: Apply a thin layer of penciclovir cream directly to the cold sore and the skin right around it. Use only on the lips and face — do NOT put it inside your mouth, nose, eyes, or on genital areas. Wash your hands before and after applying the cream. Do not cover the area with a bandage unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid getting the cream in or near your eyes, as it can cause irritation.
dosing: Apply the cream every 2 hours while you are awake for 4 days straight. Start using it as soon as you notice the first signs of a cold sore, such as tingling, itching, or redness — the sooner you start, the better it works.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. Then continue on your regular schedule of every 2 hours while awake. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed dose. If it is almost time for your next application, just skip the missed one and continue as usual.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the cream after the expiration date printed on the tube.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching your cold sore and then touching your eyes, genitals, or other people — this can spread the virus. Do not share your cream, lip balm, towels, utensils, or kiss anyone while you have an active cold sore. Avoid sunlight and UV light on your cold sore, as this can trigger outbreaks. Do not use other creams, cosmetics, or lip products on top of the treated area without asking your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if: your cold sore does not improve or gets worse after 4 days of treatment; you develop a rash, swelling, or severe skin irritation at the application site; your cold sores are spreading or happening much more often than usual; you have a weakened immune system (such as from HIV or cancer treatment) and develop a cold sore; you accidentally get the cream in your eyes; or you have any signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face.
when_it_works: Penciclovir works best when you start using it at the very first sign of a cold sore, like tingling or itching. Most people see improvement within 4 days. It can shorten the healing time by about half a day to one day. It will not completely prevent cold sores from coming back in the future.
special_populations: Children: Safety and effectiveness in children under 12 years old has not been established. Ask your doctor before using in children. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medication. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but use with care and follow your doctor's instructions. Patients with weak immune systems: If you have HIV, are on chemotherapy, or have any condition that weakens your immune system, talk to your doctor before using penciclovir, as you may need a different or stronger treatment.
